root_cause: SampleBuffer::append checks `size_ > capacity_` before writing data_[size_]. When the buffer is exactly full (size_ == capacity_) the check passes and the sample is written one element past the end of the heap storage of capacity_ ints: AddressSanitizer reports a heap-buffer-overflow WRITE of size 4 at src/sample_buffer.cpp:14 in lc::SampleBuffer::append(int) for the fill_to_capacity and capacity_one test cases.
rationale: Reject the append when size_ >= capacity_ (the buffer is full), which is exactly the documented contract (false and contents unchanged when size() == capacity()). The write data_[size_] then only happens for size_ < capacity_, i.e. inside the allocation. No other behaviour changes.
